literal: The Chen general Wu Mingche attacked Huainan; Liyang and Guabu fell in succession.
idiomatic: Chen general Wu Mingche took Huainan; Liyang and Guabu fell in turn.

literal: Zhao Yanshen at the Palace Secretariat secretly consulted Wenzong on plans to resist.
idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen secretly asked Wenzong at the Secretariat how to resist.

literal: Wenzong said: "The state's treatment of Huainan has lost it as easily as an arrow in the weeds."
idiomatic: Wenzong said, "We treat Huainan like an arrow lost in weeds."

literal: He thought Huainan ought to be entrusted to Wang Lin.
idiomatic: He thought Huainan should go to Wang Lin.

literal: Lin at Tanling plainly would not bow north to Ming.
idiomatic: Lin at Tanling would never bow north to Chen Ming.

literal: Yanshen said: "Brother, this is a fine plan.
idiomatic: Yanshen said, "A fine plan, brother.

literal: But to argue with words for ten days already went unheard.
idiomatic: Ten days of talk already failed.

literal: Affairs are as they are—how can one speak everything!"
idiomatic: Things are as they are—how can one say it all!"

literal: They then looked at each other and wept.
idiomatic: They wept together.

literal: When Qi fell, with Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others he entered the capital and was made General of the Fourth Rank, Grand Master of the Academy.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered the capital with Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others as Fourth-rank General and Academy Grand Master.

literal: In Sui's Kaihuang era he was made Juzhou Inspector.
idiomatic: In Kaihuang he was Juzhou Inspector.

literal: He fell ill, left office, and died.
idiomatic: Illness forced retirement; he died.

literal: Wenzong as a nobleman's son rose in the court ranks; his talent and judgment were quick and he was known for practical capacity.
idiomatic: A noble's son, he rose fast; quick and capable, he was known for getting things done.

literal: Yet he loved visiting the houses of the great; opinion held he was good at currying favor.
idiomatic: Yet he courted the powerful; opinion said he knew how to flatter.

literal: Son Shi, styled Jianyan.
idiomatic: Son Shi, styled Jianyan.

literal: From youth he was known; sharp in debate and with insight, he especially prided himself on clerical affairs.
idiomatic: Known from youth, sharp and insightful, he especially trusted his skill in office work.

literal: In Qi he was Left Outer Military Gentleman and also handled the Ancestral Temples Bureau.
idiomatic: In Qi he was Left Outer Military Gentleman and handled the temples bureau.

literal: Later in midsummer, because the Dragon Star appeared, rain sacrifice was requested.
idiomatic: In midsummer the Dragon Star appeared and rain sacrifice was requested.

literal: At the time Gao Anagong was Recorder of the Masters of Writing and said a true dragon had appeared, greatly delighted.
idiomatic: Gao Anagong, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, said a real dragon had appeared and rejoiced.

literal: He asked where the dragon was and what color it was.
idiomatic: He asked where it was and what color.

literal: Shi composed himself and said: "This is the Dragon Star's first appearance; by rite rain sacrifice is at the suburban altar—it does not mean a true dragon has descended elsewhere."
idiomatic: Shi said calmly, "This is the Dragon Star's first sighting; rite calls for suburban rain sacrifice—not a dragon descending elsewhere."

literal: Anagong flushed angrily and said: "Han fellows meddle too much, pretending to know the stars!"
idiomatic: Anagong snapped, "Han meddlers, pretending to know the stars!"

literal: The sacrifice was not performed.
idiomatic: The rite was dropped.

literal: Shi left and sighed in private: "The state's great affairs lie in sacrifice and arms; when rites are abandoned, can it last long?
idiomatic: Leaving, he sighed, "Sacrifice and arms are the state's root; rites abandoned—how long can it last?

literal: Qi's fall is not far!"
idiomatic: Qi has no days left!"

literal: Soon Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi and made him Superior Tax Master.
idiomatic: Soon Zhou Wu pacified Qi and made him Superior Tax Master.

literal: When Sui Wendi received the mandate he rose in succession to Left Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing and was famed for clarity and efficiency.
idiomatic: When Wendi took the throne he rose to Left Assistant Minister, famed for clarity and drive.

literal: At the time Prince of Shu Xiu often violated law; Shi was made Staff Major to the Yizhou Regional Commander.
idiomatic: Prince of Shu Xiu broke the law; Shi was made Yizhou staff major.

literal: Before long Xiu was summoned; fearing trouble in the capital, he meant to plead illness.
idiomatic: Soon Xiu was summoned; fearing the capital, he would plead illness.

literal: Shi repeatedly urged him that he could not defy the command.
idiomatic: Shi urged him not to defy the order.

literal: Xiu then flushed and said: "This is my family's affair—what has it to do with you?"
idiomatic: Xiu snapped, "Family business—none of your affair!"

literal: Shi wept and admonished bitterly; Xiu then followed the summons.
idiomatic: Shi wept and pleaded; Xiu went.

literal: After Xiu's hair was removed many prefectural officials were implicated; Shi was spared for this.
idiomatic: After Xiu was punished many officials were implicated; Shi was spared.

literal: Later he was made General of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: Later Third-rank General.

literal: In office Shi was forceful and clear, with a ready tongue, but had no name for integrity and fairness.
idiomatic: In office he was forceful and sharp-tongued but not called fair.

literal: He died as Vice Minister of Punishments.
idiomatic: He died as Vice Minister of Punishments.

literal: Zigong's younger brother Zizuan, styled Lingxiu, held post of Vice Grand Steward.
idiomatic: Younger brother Zizuan, styled Lingxiu, was Vice Grand Steward.

literal: He was killed at Heyin; posthumously Qinzhou Inspector.
idiomatic: Killed at Heyin; posthumously Qinzhou Inspector.

literal: Son Xiong.
idiomatic: Son Xiong.

literal: Xiong, styled Shilüe, from youth was generous and of fine appearance.
idiomatic: Xiong, styled Shilüe, was generous and handsome from youth.

literal: He first served Wei and rose to Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: He first served Wei as Secretariat Gentleman.

literal: Under Zhou, for merit in the Qi campaign he was enfeoffed Duke of Shuo and was successively Jizhou and Pingzhou Inspector and Acting Xuzhou Regional Commander.
idiomatic: Under Zhou, for the Qi campaign he was Duke of Shuo, then Jizhou and Pingzhou Inspector and acting Xuzhou commander.

literal: When Yuwen Jiong rebelled, Xiong's family dependents were at Xiangzhou and Jiong secretly sent a letter to entice him.
idiomatic: When Yuwen Jiong rebelled, Xiong's family was at Xiangzhou and Jiong secretly wrote to win him.

literal: Xiong in the end paid no heed.
idiomatic: Xiong ignored it.

literal: Sui Wendi sent a letter to comfort and encourage him.
idiomatic: Wendi sent a letter of comfort.

literal: Jiong sent his general Bi Yixu to hold Lanling; Xi Pi took the lower town of Changyu; Xiong sent troops and pacified all.
idiomatic: Jiong's Bi Yixu held Lanling; Xi Pi took Changyu's lower town; Xiong's troops cleared both.

literal: The Chen, seeing the central plains in turmoil, sent generals Chen Ji, Xiao Mohe, Ren Mannu, Zhou Luozi, Fan Yi, and others to invade north of the river.
idiomatic: Chen sent Chen Ji, Xiao Mohe, Ren Mannu, Zhou Luozi, and Fan Yi north while the plains were in turmoil.

literal: From Jiangling east to Shouyang many responded; they attacked and took towns and forts.
idiomatic: From Jiangling to Shouyang many joined them and took towns.

literal: Xiong with Wu Regional Commander Yu Yi and others drove them off.
idiomatic: Xiong with Yu Yi of Wu and others drove them off.

literal: All former territory was recovered.
idiomatic: All lost ground was recovered.

literal: He advanced to Grand General and was made Xuzhou Regional Commander, then transferred to Shuo Regional Commander.
idiomatic: He became Grand General, Xuzhou commander, then Shuo commander.

literal: In the pacification of Chen he followed Prince Qin Jun by the Xinzhou route.
idiomatic: Pacifying Chen, he followed Prince Qin Jun on the Xinzhou road.

literal: When Chen was pacified, for merit he advanced to Pillar of State, enfeoffed son Chong Baron of Duanshi and Bao Baron of Anhua, and again held Shuo.
idiomatic: Chen pacified, he was Pillar of State; sons Chong and Bao were barons; he again held Shuo.

literal: The next year he memorialized asking to retire; summoned back to the capital, he died at home.
idiomatic: Next year he asked to retire, was recalled, and died at home.

literal: Son Song inherited; in the Daye era he was Director of the Parks Bureau and campaigned against the Beihai rebels.
idiomatic: Son Song inherited; in Daye he was Parks Director and fought Beihai rebels.

literal: He died fighting hard; posthumously Proper Counselor.
idiomatic: He died in hard fighting; posthumously Proper Counselor.

literal: Liu Ni, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Liu Ni, of Dai.

literal: Great-grandfather Dun had merit under Emperor Daowu and was a frontier great chief.
idiomatic: Great-grandfather Dun served Daowu and was a frontier great chief.

literal: Father Lou was Champion General.
idiomatic: Father Lou was Champion General.

literal: Ni was brave, decisive, and skilled at archery; Taiwu saw him and favored him, made him Gentlemen of the Feathered Forest, and enfeoffed him Viscount of Chang.
idiomatic: Brave and skilled at archery, Taiwu favored him, made him Feathered Forest gentleman, and enfeoffed Viscount of Chang.

literal: When Zong Ai had killed Prince of Nan'an Yu at the eastern temple and kept it secret, only Ni knew the circumstances.
idiomatic: When Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an Yu at the eastern temple and hid it, only Ni knew.

literal: Ni urged Ai to enthrone Wencheng.
idiomatic: Ni urged Ai to enthrone Wencheng.

literal: Ai himself thought he had sinned against Jingmu and, hearing this, said in alarm: "You are a great fool!
idiomatic: Ai, guilty toward Jingmu, cried, "You great fool!

literal: If the imperial grandson is enthroned, will he not remember the Zhengping affair?"
idiomatic: Enthrone the grandson and he will remember Zhengping!"

literal: Ni said: "If so, whom shall we enthrone?"
idiomatic: Ni said, "Then whom do we enthrone?"

literal: Ai said: "Wait until we return to the palace and choose the worthy among the princes' sons."
idiomatic: Ai said, "Wait till we return and pick a worthy prince's son."

literal: Ni feared he would change course and secretly reported the situation to Palace Attendant Yuan He.
idiomatic: Fearing a change, Ni secretly told Palace Attendant Yuan He.

literal: At the time he and Ni together commanded troops on night guard; they then with Southern Department Director Lu Li plotted and secretly supported the imperial grandson.
idiomatic: He and Ni then held night guard; with Lu Li they secretly backed the grandson.

literal: Thereupon He with Masters of Writing Director Changsun Kehou arrayed troops in strict guard; Ni with Li welcomed Wencheng from the park.
idiomatic: He and Changsun Kehou guarded with troops; Ni and Li brought Wencheng from the park.

literal: Li held Wencheng in his arms on horseback and entered the capital.
idiomatic: Li carried Wencheng on horseback into the capital.

literal: Ni galloped back to the eastern temple and shouted: "Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an—great treason!
idiomatic: Ni galloped to the eastern temple and shouted, "Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an—treason!

literal: The imperial grandson has already ascended."
idiomatic: The grandson is already enthroned."

literal: There is an edict: all night-guard troops may return to the palace."
idiomatic: Edict: night guard, return to the palace."

literal: The crowd all shouted ten thousand years.
idiomatic: All shouted long life.

literal: He and Kehou seized Zong Ai, Jia Zhou, and others, led troops in, and at the palace gate supported Wencheng; he entered and ascended Yong'an Hall.
idiomatic: He and Kehou seized Zong Ai and Jia Zhou, led troops in, and enthroned Wencheng at Yong'an Hall.

literal: Ni was made Inner Chief and enfeoffed Duke of Dong'an.
idiomatic: Ni was Inner Chief and Duke of Dong'an.

literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and made Qinzhou Inspector.
idiomatic: Soon Vice Director and Qinzhou Inspector.

literal: In the province he was pure and cautious, yet often drunk.
idiomatic: In office he was pure but often drunk.

literal: At the end of Wencheng he was Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Late in Wencheng he was Minister of Works.

literal: When Xianwen ascended, because Ni had great merit in the former reign he was given special respect and granted forty separate households.
idiomatic: Xianwen gave him special honor and forty separate households for past merit.

literal: In the fourth year of Huangxing the imperial carriage campaigned north; the emperor personally swore the host, but Ni was drunk and the battle array was not in order.
idiomatic: Huangxing 4 the emperor campaigned north and swore the troops; Ni was drunk and the ranks were disorderly.

literal: The emperor, because his merit was weighty, especially pardoned him and only removed him from office.
idiomatic: For his great merit the emperor only dismissed him.

literal: In the fourth year of Yanxing he died; son She Sheng inherited.
idiomatic: Yanxing 4 he died; son She Sheng inherited.

literal: Discussion: Lu Si was famed for wisdom and discernment; Yu did not fall short of the family style, upheld name and integrity by principle, and built his own fame;
idiomatic: Commentary: Lu Si was famed for wisdom; Yu kept the family style, upheld integrity, and made his own name;

literal: His fragrance in records and canons—was it for nothing?
idiomatic: His fame in records—was it empty?

literal: Li was loyal to state and lord, a pillar of the realm.
idiomatic: Li served state and lord—a pillar of the realm.

literal: With loyalty and righteousness he went to hardship as homeward; generations prospered—fame was not empty.
idiomatic: Loyal and righteous, he met hardship like home; the house flourished—fame was earned.

literal: Rui and Xiu rose through calm elegance—why at the end did they run wild?
idiomatic: Rui and Xiu rose by calm grace—why run wild at the end?

literal: Zizhang's fine end—family renown greatly stirred.
idiomatic: Zizhang's good death shook the family name.

literal: Yang and Yanshi both took filial piety as root; fame in coming forth and withdrawal both could model human relations.
idiomatic: Yang and Yanshi rooted in filial piety—coming forth or staying back, both could model the world.

literal: Shuang's learning had a name—also men's praise.
idiomatic: Shuang's scholarship was heard—men praised him too.

literal: Yuan He was imposing—not only martial bearing; see how he aided Wencheng on the throne, checked abdication in court—nearly a minister of the altars.
idiomatic: Yuan He was imposing—not mere martial show; he raised Wencheng and checked abdication in court—a pillar of the state.

literal: Huai combined strategy and talent, fame inside and out, followed worthy traces without failing forebears.
idiomatic: Huai joined strategy and talent, won fame at court and border, and did not shame his fathers.

literal: Ziyong's merit stood in the Xia regions; he died on the Jizhou plain.
idiomatic: Ziyong won the Xia frontier and died in Jizhou fields.

literal: Biao was famed in Qi.
idiomatic: Biao shone in Qi.

literal: Shi and Xiong's offices matured in Sui—beautiful.
idiomatic: Shi and Xiong finished their careers in Sui—fine indeed.

literal: Liu Ni was loyal to the state—was it only for fierce valor?
idiomatic: Liu Ni served the state—was it only for fighting?

literal: Xue Ti's upright counsel and loyal plot met harm from villainous eunuchs—painful!
idiomatic: Xue Ti's loyal counsel died at eunuch hands—how painful!
